text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL TO PAY $17.5 BILLION IN FOREIGN DEBT
Brazil will pay $17.5 million this year to amortize the principal on its mid-term public and private foreign debt, up roughly 50 percent from last year.
-- DOLLAR IN-FLOWS TO BRAZIL BOLSAS RISE
The rate at which foreign capital is entering Brazilian stock markets has risen in 1997. Figures from the Sao Paulo bolsa show net dollar in-flows reached $296.28 million in January's first 10 days.
-- GOVERNMENT-ALLIED PARTIES STAKE OUT POSITIONS
The on-going debate on re-election is allowing the parties allied to Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to clearly stake out their positions and interests in Congress.
O GLOBO
-- PANEL OKs RE-ELECTION; PMDB PARTY, CARDOSO BEGIN TALKS

With the help of six PMDB party members, the government succeeded in getting a special congressional committee to pass a re-election amendment, forcing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to negotiate with the party.
-- LAWMAKER DEFENDS SHOOTING OF THREE LANDLESS FARMERS

Brazilian congressman Dep. Giovanni Queiroz, cousin of the owner of a ranch where three landless farmers were slain in a clash earlier this week, defended the right of ranchowners to defend with arms their property.
-- GETULIO VARGAS'S SON IMMITATES FATHER'S SUICIDE
Maneco Vargas, the youngest son of former president Getulio Vargas, immitated his father's suicide 42 years earlier by shooting himself in the heart.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT GIVES IN TO PMDB AND DELAYS RE-ELECTION

Brazil's government has acceded to the demands of the the PMDB, the largest party in Congress, and delayed its schedule for approval of an amendment that would allow President Fernando Henrique to run for re-election n 1998.
-- PERUVIAN GUERRILLAS AGREE TO NEGOTIATE
Marxist guerrillas holding 74 hostages at the Japanese ambassadors home in Lima have agreed to take part in talks with the Peruvian government to end the 29-day crisis.
-- SLAIN LANDLESS WERE SHOT FROM HALF METER AWAY

The shots that killed three landless peasants in a clash with armed guards at a ranch in northern Para state this week were shot in the chest with a 38-calibre revolver from half a meter away, Brazilian forensic experts said.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
